title: Freya and the Extraction
premise: Casper Zhou has spent three years as the invisible guardian of a safe house protecting a witness to a biotech conglomerate's crimes, but when the property appears on a real estate site with interior photos, she realizes someone inside her own security firm sold them out. The listing is a message: the 'accident' meant to erase the witness and everyone guarding him is scheduled for days from now. Casper must unmask the mole, move the witness through a city that suddenly knows her face, and confront the truth that her employer, Halcyon Detail, orchestrated the leak to collect an insurance payout on its most expensive liability. In the end she burns her polished lie, trades her invisibility for testimony, and walks away with nothing but the memory of who she used to be — and the inheritance of a choice her father made decades ago in the same trade.
about_author: Lior Vasquez is a former risk analyst who spent six years writing threat assessments for private security firms before turning to fiction. They live in Lisbon, where they write about the people paid to stay unseen.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: POV Casper. During a routine supply run, Casper finds the safe house listed online — twelve photos of rooms only four people have ever entered, including her bedroom and the witness's medication cabinet. She returns to find her team leader, Brandt, oddly calm. Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing your hidden life has been catalogued and priced.

chapters.title: Household of Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Flashback threads reveal how Casper inherited this job from her father, a legendary contractor who vanished mid-contract years ago. She audits the team: Brandt, tech specialist Ivo, and the witness, Dr. Amara Sen, whose memory is failing from early dementia — the living archive of Halcyon's crimes. Beat: dread braided with tenderness.

chapters.title: Twelve Photographs
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Analyzing the photos, Casper notices one was taken from an angle only reachable during a scheduled maintenance window — meaning someone on rotation leaked access. Ivo's alibi doesn't hold. Meanwhile Dr. Sen mistakes Casper for her dead daughter and confides a fragment: a date, a name, 'Vasquez.' Beat: paranoia tightening like a wire.

chapters.title: Open House
chapters.summary: POV alternating Casper and a stranger casing the neighborhood. A couple tours the still-occupied house; Casper watches from across the street and recognizes the 'buyer' as a Halcyon fixer named Rell. The showing confirms it: the sale is theater, the attack is real, and the timeline is under two weeks. Beat: cold clarity replacing denial.

chapters.title: Go-Bag Ethics
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper prepares extraction routes but hesitates — running means abandoning proof and confirming Halcyon's story that Sen is unstable. She contacts her father's old handler, Yusra, who warns that Casper's father discovered the same insurance scheme before he disappeared. Beat: the pull between survival and duty, inheritance as burden.

chapters.title: What Amara Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Dr. Sen. Through Sen's fracturing memory we see the original crime: a trial drug suppressed, a village of data points erased, and Halcyon executives deciding a fire would be cleaner than a lawsuit. Sen hides evidence fragments in places her disease will forget but the house won't. Beat: grief for a mind becoming a locked room.

chapters.title: The Mole's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper traps Ivo with a falsified schedule and he confesses — not to betrayal but to debt, coerced by Rell after Halcyon flagged him. He gives her the attack plan: a gas 'leak' timed to a utility inspection, ten days out. Brandt, she learns, signed off knowingly. Beat: betrayal reframed as corruption spreading downward.

chapters.title: Ten Days
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Moving Sen through the city using tourist crowds and a decommissioned tram depot, Casper is made by Rell's surveillance net. A near-miss chase ends with Ivo shot covering their escape — alive but captured, and now a loose end who can name her. Beat: adrenaline curdling into guilt.

chapters.title: Accident Weather
chapters.summary: POV Casper. With nowhere left to hide, Casper flips the script: she lets Halcyon believe Sen is back at the safe house while she delivers the real Sen — and her father's recovered evidence cache — to a journalist and a federal prosecutor Yusra trusts. Rell springs the trap on an empty house rigged to expose his crew instead. Beat: the hunted becoming the architect.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: POV Casper, weeks later. Testimony begins; Halcyon's executives fall, though the machine itself survives. Casper learns her father didn't vanish — he took a payout and a new name, and chose, at the end, to send her the evidence instead of silence. She unpacks the go-bag for the first time in years. Beat: quiet reckoning; power corrupts, but memory can be refused.
